summary: INT3A (2026-11-28): reward integration fixes (docs/INT3A.md): LRN-3 bootstrap inputs written (reward_signals.<name> annotation keys read by assemble.stored_signals; exploration and learning-progress components non-zero in the inner update); KF-E01 stored credit reaches the policy-improvement goal term (simple per decision where outcomes are attributed; RUDDER / COCOA return-to-go replaces the discounted goal return), verified by G2-learn (G2L-7); KF-E02 info_gain read from info_gain_nats; KF-E05 R_psi's lifetime context carries across objectives (MetaLearner.new_objective); LRN-6 regression test; promotion-test power analysis: conclusive only for an effect of the order of the utility's RMS at realistic evidence rates (~3,400 held-out groups for 80 % power at no effect), no defect found, mix not forced. || Stage 1 + stage 2. The learned intrinsic reward R_psi and its lifetime meta-gradient are implemented end to end on the real model at debug scale: PolicyImprovementLoss (one function used as the learner's LossProvider with R_psi detached and, functionally over the policy head + decision trunk, as the inner step of the unroll); MetaLearner (real policy updates with snapshots, support/query windows inside one lifetime, utilities only from a hash-chained ledger of signed outcomes, on-policy or importance-weighted outer step, held-out promotion of the bootstrap mix, MetaUpdateRecord also for skipped updates); signal assembly with a documented source for every signal; a budgeted goal-free mode on the fast posterior; integrity guards. The mathematics checks out (finite differences, exact zeros under the two ablations, psi bit-identical under the inner loss). The science does not: in the multi-lifetime LabWorld comparison (10 seeds x 320 lifetimes, re-run after the G-pr fixes) the learned reward used from scratch: hurt relative to bootstrap-only (-0.350 [-0.430, -0.270] in verified goal achievement; it collapsed onto a non-intervention in 3 of 10 seeds and ended low in the others), and the cold-start path: no detectable difference relative to bootstrap-only (-0.038 [-0.186, +0.111]). No learning result here comes from live or staging experience; the integrated agent (agent.py, M-int) now calls MetaLearner and GoalFreeMode but needs change requests C-10 / C-11 for the fixed admission and budget rules. G-pr fixes (docs/C/FIXES.md): return-to-go baseline no longer depends on the row's own outcome (D1, exact unbiasedness test); outer utilities derived in the ledger from the signed outcome, caller utilities / credits refused and chained (D2); only objectives with a recorded operator origin supervise (D3); goal-free budget counts pending goals (D4); reworded self-goals discounted (D6); on-policy estimator only when the live update replays bit-identically (D7); anchored ledger (D8); 'bootstrap' label until a promoted meta-update (D12); a zero / non-finite meta-gradient or unchanged psi is never recorded as applied (M-int staging run 2). The LabWorld experiment was re-run in full on the fixed, committed code. | LRN round (S-5, 2026-11-27): selection rule thompson_policy (Thompson sampling over the world model's posterior + a policy correction weighted by a calibration on verified outcomes), policy-improvement loss with a goal term and an all-candidate model term, trust-region live step, reward components standardised before mixing, promotion as a non-inferiority test, delta V / verified-delta fixes; docs/C/LRN_S5.md, docs/evidence/B/choice_summary.json, docs/evidence/C/lrn_probes_*.json; JUnit docs/evidence/test_results/LRN.xml (298 passed, 13 skipped).

not_done: Integration: cam_live/agent.py and the runtime do not call any of this yet. AgentAPI.internal_rewards -> MetaLearner.internal_rewards, AgentAPI.meta_learn -> MetaLearner.meta_update, verifier outcomes -> MetaLearner.admit_objective, checkpoint -> MetaLearner.state_dict, and who applies the policy-improvement step (change request C-8) are the master's to wire.

No live or staging experience. Every learning result is from LabWorld (diagnostic provenance) on CamLiveConfig.debug(): a tiny random backbone and an untrained debug core, where candidate actions differ almost only by operation type (cosine 0.99 between interventions on different channels). The Qwen3-4B / 50m run measured cost only; no learning was attempted at that scale.

The predict workstream's trained heads were not in the loop of the experiment: success estimate, delta V, action quality, VOI, information gain, epistemic uncertainty and prediction error were masked, so R_psi saw latents, costs, elapsed time, execution status and verified progress only, and the bootstrap reward reduced to its verified-outcome component.

No remedy for the collapse of the learned-reward learner was tried (exploration floor in the acting rule, entropy schedule, resetting theta per lifetime, slower promotion). The inner learning rate and entropy bonus were picked on seeds 0-2 (160 lifetimes) by the bootstrap and verified-outcome learners' results; the reported seeds 10-19 were not used for tuning.
The promotion rule is uncalibrated: non-inferiority margin (0.01 utility units), step (0.25) and held-out fraction (0.25) were set by hand.
Lifetime value beyond the truncation window (Zheng et al. Eq. 5-6) is not implemented; intrinsic returns stop at the end of the support batch.

Truncation bias, importance-weight clipping bias and the multi-event unroll (unroll_events > 1, inner-data score term) are not quantified on the real model; the multi-event path has one functional test.
K = 8 is not checked against finite differences on the real model (stage-1 diagnostics only).

Verifier measurements cannot supervise in live operation until contracts.OutcomeObservation carries a signature or the verifier supplies check_measurement (change request C-1); only signed VerifiedOutcome records can.
Goal-free mode: not called by the runtime; needs (action, query) pairs from the candidate generators; expected transferable competence is a constant; real-valued queries only in the tests.
MetaLearner's bookkeeping maps (decision -> lifetime, used rows, lifetime-context snapshots) grow with the lifetime and are not pruned.
Detection of engagement statistics without genuine participation is verifier-side and not covered here.
Reverse-over-forward Hessian-vector products for the adjoint sweep are not implemented (double backward is used).

G-pr fixes need two integration changes in agent.py (M-int): register the assigned TaskSpec with MetaLearner.register_objective (C-10; until then the agent's objective outcomes are refused for the meta ledger, fail closed) and abandon proposed goal-free goals that are not executed (C-11; until then goal-free mode stops selecting once pending goals hold the budget). Signing the objective origin by the verifier is proposed as C-12.

Semantic near-duplicate self-goals: SelfGoalDiscount(embed=...) exists, but on the real Qwen3-4B text embedding no threshold separates rewordings from different goals; only the lexical fold is on by default.
LRN: bootstrap learning progress / epistemic reduction have no input in runtime runs (agent does not write them; LRN-3).
LRN: the promotion margin (0.05 x utility RMS), step (0.25) and 4-group minimum are set by hand, not calibrated.
LRN: a refused checkpoint promotion rolls back psi and the policy head with everything else (LRN-6, INT2 / D); in the real-model run this undid the applied meta-step before the next live update.

LRN: on the real configuration the live update was changed by a meta-step only with the mix fixed at 0.5 and checkpoint rollback off (pathway check); in the default configuration the mix stayed 1 in the 5-lifetime run.

INT3A: The bootstrap mix stays at 1 at realistic evidence rates by design of the promotion test (cleared buffer of ~4-6 groups per decision); a sequential bound pooling evidence would be a design change (not made).
INT3A: Whether LRN-3's exploration / learning-progress terms or the credit-based goal term improve behaviour is not measured.

Adjoint checkpointing buys little at the 50m preset: at K = 2 it uses more memory than the full unroll (221 vs 198 MB) and 1.5x the time; at K = 4 it saves 23 % memory (265 vs 343 MB) for 1.4x the time.

(stage 1) First-order approximation is not a validated lower-cost approximation: relative error against the exact window gradient 13 % / 30 % / 46 % at K = 2 / 4 / 8 (bandit MLP, inner_lr 0.5, normalised advantages) and it used more peak memory than the full unroll at K = 8 in all three cost configurations (e.g. 698 vs 477 MiB at 10M theta). Kept for comparison only.

(stage 1) Adjoint checkpointing does not reduce memory when parameter tensors dominate: 529 vs 477 MiB at K = 8 with 10M theta and 64 rows per step, at 2.5x the time. It helps only when activations dominate (184 vs 479 MiB at 2048 rows per step, 1.9x the time).

(stage 1) The meta-learned reward does not beat an extrinsic reward whose magnitude is tuned by an oracle when the learner takes exact updates: held-out key-to-door, J after 3 updates 1.005 (learned, scale-matched) vs 1.049 (extrinsic x32) vs 0.728 (extrinsic). It does beat the extrinsic reward at equal step size and magnitude, and every step-scaled extrinsic learner (x4, x16, x32) when updates are sampled (n=4: 0.972 vs at most 0.940; n=16: 0.997 vs at most 0.993).

(stage 1) Truncated windows are strongly biased in magnitude against the full lifetime gradient: relative error 0.75 / 0.55 / 0.24 for K = 1 / 2 / 4 of an 8-update lifetime (sum objective), 0.87 / 0.75 / 0.50 (final objective), and still 0.18 / 0.49 for K = 8 of 16 updates, with cosine above 0.999 throughout.

(stage 1) With very small inner batches the sampled-inner-update objective itself differs from the exact-update objective: gradient gap 9-22 % at n_inner <= 2 on the test tree (below 3 % at n_inner = 16).
